title: Canonical and other religious-order Eucharistic book states

traditions.label: Premonstratensian use
traditions.coverage_note: Selected scholarly descriptions of substantive changes; full direct original-book collation remains incomplete.

traditions.label: Gilbertine use
traditions.scope: Medieval Gilbertine Eucharistic books, with Lincoln 115 and Cambridge St John 239 kept distinct.
traditions.coverage_note: A 1921–1922 critical edition supports manuscript layers; its publication dates are not medieval revision dates.

traditions.label: Pauline use
traditions.scope: Order of Saint Paul the First Hermit; Hungarian and related Central European houses.
traditions.coverage_note: Order-use and local diocesan adaptations distinguished; unrelated to Paul VI.

traditions.label: Windesheim Canons Regular
traditions.scope: Congregation and the Frankenthal witness Vatican Pal. lat. 479.
traditions.coverage_note: Not a universal Augustinian rite. Office-only origin records do not become Mass books.

traditions.label: Teutonic Order
traditions.scope: Order Mass books and proper supplements, with regional and language scope explicit.
traditions.coverage_note: Medieval permission, printed witness and modern regional proper are different historical evidence classes.

sources.limitations: Manuscript dating, layering and house attribution are Woolley’s scholarly judgments, not fresh palaeographic inspection. Volume I contains the Ordinal and Office of St Gilbert; its introduction discusses the Eucharistic manuscripts.

stages.label: Lincoln Cathedral MS 115: original Mass-prayer collection
stages.scope: Original central Mass-prayer collection, not the composite manuscript’s later material. The comparison includes an early marginal Thomas collect, distinguished from the original hand. Lectionary scope records the editor’s stated absence of lessons in the named core formularies, for comparison with their supplied Appendix lessons.
stages.witness_label: Lincoln Cathedral MS 115: original Mass-prayer collection
stages.summary: Temporal, sanctoral and common Mass prayers form the original core; an Ambrosian preparation prayer is contemporary.

evidence.claim: Woolley separates the original late 12th-century collection from appended and prefixed supplements.

stages.limitations: Late-century/approximate dates are Woolley’s palaeographic and internal-evidence judgments. No medieval promulgation date or universal house reception established. The marginal Thomas collect is a near-contemporary addition, not part of the original hand.
stages.reception: Possible Saint Katherine, Lincoln attribution is argued by the editor, not an order-wide decree.

stages.label: Lincoln MS 115: appended Mass supplement
stages.scope: Gradual addition of sung parts and lessons to the original prayer book.
stages.summary: An appended supplement supplies choir parts and lessons; Hugh and William of York Masses help date completion around 1230.

evidence.claim: Editor describes supplementation and dating from canonizations 1220 and 1227.

stages.limitations: Woolley describes gradual accumulation and approximate completion around 1230; the point coordinate is not an exact copying date. He allows the extreme end of the Appendix to postdate the prefixed Supplement. These layers do not form a clean nonoverlapping succession, and no order-wide promulgation or reception is established.
stages.reception: Publication or witness survival does not establish uniform reception across houses.

stages.label: Lincoln MS 115: prefixed Gilbertine supplement
stages.date_label: Towards the end of the first half of the thirteenth century, before 1250; before 1247 inferred by Woolley
stages.scope: New prefixed collection of special Masses; later Edmund addition kept separate.
stages.summary: A prefixed supplement replaces portions of the appendix and gives Thomas of Canterbury a proper collect in place of the earlier marginal collect from the common for a martyr bishop.

evidence.claim: Woolley describes ordering and replacement; before 1247 is his inference from later Edmund addition.
Printed Thomas formulary in the prefixed collection is visible.

stages.limitations: Late-century/approximate dates are Woolley’s palaeographic and internal-evidence judgments. No medieval promulgation date or universal house reception established. Before 1247 is a qualified inference, not a secure terminus from an act.
stages.reception: Publication or witness survival does not establish uniform reception across houses.

stages.label: St John’s College Cambridge MS 239: Canon and special Gilbertine Masses
stages.scope: Calendar at fol. 3b; Canon, prefaces and special Masses at fols. 381–388b, within a composite Calendar/Bible/liturgical volume.
stages.witness_label: St John’s College Cambridge MS 239: Canon and special Gilbertine Masses
stages.summary: The Canon, prefaces and special Masses share a hand; the shorter common and omitted local Masses distinguish it from Lincoln 115.

evidence.claim: Woolley dates the manuscript using an unfulfilled 1265 prophecy and suggests a standard book.

stages.limitations: Late-century/approximate dates are Woolley’s palaeographic and internal-evidence judgments. No medieval promulgation date or universal house reception established. The proposed standard-book function is the editor’s hypothesis.
stages.reception: Publication or witness survival does not establish uniform reception across houses.

stages.label: 1578 Missale Praemonstratense: embolism rubric
stages.summary: The priest kisses the paten during the peace petition and signs the forehead later.

evidence.claim: King quotes the 1578 rubric.

stages.limitations: Original 1578 leaf not yet collated; quotation is secondary evidence.
stages.reception: Publication or witness survival does not establish uniform reception across houses.

stages.label: Revised 1622 Premonstratensian missal
stages.scope: Mass Ordinary, Requiem readings and sequence selection.
stages.summary: Adopts the Pian Ordinary and drops the weekday cycle of Requiem lessons.

evidence.claim: King connects publication with 1618 chapter instructions.

stages.limitations: Publication and chapter instruction are distinct; original 1622 book not acquired.
stages.reception: Publication or witness survival does not establish uniform reception across houses.

stages.label: 1663 Premonstratensian missal: sequence restriction
stages.summary: Laetabundus for Christmas survives as the sole sequence outside the Pian repertory.

evidence.claim: King distinguishes 1660 chapter action from 1663 publication.

stages.limitations: Original 1663 book and chapter act not inspected.
stages.reception: Publication or witness survival does not establish uniform reception across houses.

stages.label: 1739 Ordinarius: embolism gesture
stages.scope: Ceremonial rubric in an ordinal, not a new missal.
stages.summary: The embolism follows the Urban VIII Roman rubric for kissing the paten at pacem.

evidence.claim: King compares the earlier ritual and 1739 ordinal.

stages.limitations: King’s separate report of deacon paten-raising concerns a Prémontré motherhouse custom, not a universal mandate.
stages.reception: Publication or witness survival does not establish uniform reception across houses.

stages.label: Frankenthal Windesheim Liber ordinarius, Pal. lat. 479, fascicle II
stages.scope: Fols 1r–76v: Mass/Office ceremonial and supporting chapter material.
stages.witness_label: Frankenthal Windesheim Liber ordinarius, Pal. lat. 479, fascicle II
stages.summary: The ordinal regulates Mass and includes precautions for the Canon at 68r–72r. Frankenthal had joined Windesheim in 1468.

evidence.claim: Catalogue identifies actual Eucharistic ceremonial and the revised approximate date.

stages.limitations: Catalogue evidence only. Its older missal-fragment flyleaves belong to a separate 12th-century fascicle, not the Windesheim reform. The approximate year is only a display coordinate.
stages.reception: The quoted 25v calendar provision concerns Utrecht and houses in its diocese; no universal diocesan rank is inferred.

stages.label: Ordinarius divini officii, Deventer 1521
stages.scope: Printed Windesheim ordinal, compared in the manuscript catalogue.
stages.summary: The print mostly agrees with Pal. lat. 479 but adds a calendar and omits its prologue.

evidence.claim: Catalogue identifies these book-content differences.

stages.limitations: No Mass-text revision inferred from the paratextual differences; no full 1521 scan acquired.
stages.reception: Publication or witness survival does not establish uniform reception across houses.

stages.label: First printed Pauline missal, Basel, ca. 1490
stages.scope: Missale Eremitarum Ordinis S. Pauli, GWM23909, especially prefaces.
stages.witness_label: First printed Pauline missal, Basel, ca. 1490
stages.summary: The Pauline print has 15 preface placements for 11 distinct texts; Esztergom 1484 has 12 placements for 11 texts. Marian feast clauses differ.

evidence.claim: Scholar distinguishes textual number from repeated placements and melodies.
Approximate typographic attribution and copy-specific Zagreb 1521 inscription are distinguished from publication and normative revision.

stages.limitations: Ca. 1490 is a typographic attribution; the approximate year is only a display coordinate. Comparison with Esztergom establishes affinity and differences, not descent from the 1484 printing.
stages.reception: Handwritten music differs among surviving copies. Zagreb copy records local-use language in 1521; this does not redefine the universal order use.

stages.label: Missale Paulinum, Venice, Petrus Liechtenstein, 1514
stages.scope: Original Latin order missal, OSZK RMK III 0196.
stages.summary: Petrus Liechtenstein printing is identified explicitly with the Order of Saint Paul the First Hermit.

evidence.claim: Detailed catalogue distinguishes Ordinary, prefaces, Canon andcolophon.

stages.limitations: Catalogue-only witness; inaccessible PDF prevents a substantive revision claim.
stages.reception: Publication or witness survival does not establish uniform reception across houses.

stages.label: Missale Dominorum Teutonicorum, Nuremberg, ca. 1499
stages.scope: Latin missal, BSB 2 Inc.s.a.880m, GW M24184.
stages.summary: An identifiable printed order missal survives in the BSB collection.

evidence.claim: The catalogue dates the Stuchs printing approximately 1499.

stages.limitations: Approximate date has a point display coordinate; it is not a precise publication day or normative act.
stages.reception: The order’s retrospective reports Innocent IV’s permission to adopt Dominican Mass and Office on 13 February 1244 and Alexander IV’s confirmation of adaptations on 27 February 1257. These permissions do not identify a surviving 1244 book or demonstrate uniform house implementation.

stages.label: Pustet order proper and calendar
stages.scope: Proper texts and calendar, not a distinct complete Mass rite.
stages.summary: Roman approvals in 1902–1903 preceded the 1903 printing; new foundation and Elisabeth texts were prepared.

evidence.claim: Order account separates approvals and Pustet publication.

stages.limitations: The official retrospective explicitly identifies a proper for Mass and Breviary, alongside the calendar. The original book has not been acquired and its exact textual contents remain uncollated.
stages.reception: Publication or witness survival does not establish uniform reception across houses.

stages.label: German-language Teutonic Mass proper
stages.scope: Brother and sister provinces of the order in the German-speaking region; regional proper supplement.
stages.summary: The proper was approved on 6 January 2003 and published in 2003. Its decree describes amended orations, ritual additions and a companion lectionary, following the Roman 1970 missal and its German 1975 translation.

evidence.claim: Title and decree distinguish regional scope, publication and 6 January 2003 authorization.

stages.limitations: Mixed regional proper with original alterations and additions, not demonstrably only a translation. Exact changed units are not collated. Independent translation history remains deferred; protected full bytes are not republished.
stages.reception: PDF 8 calendar follows the 2000 general chapter, not a separately inferred 2003 calendar reform.

transitions.summary: The Appendix adds lessons to named votive formularies represented by prayers in the Collectar.

changes.before: Prayers for named Trinity, Holy Spirit, Holy Cross and Marian votive formularies.
changes.after: The Appendix supplies lessons for these named formularies; this comparison is bounded to the editor’s table.

evidence.claim: The editor compares Collectar prayers with the Appendix’s lessons and other material for named formularies.
The editor compares Collectar prayers with the Appendix’s lessons and other material for named formularies.

transitions.limitations: Physical supplementation of this manuscript, not proof of an order-wide reform.

transitions.summary: A proper Thomas of Canterbury collect replaces the earlier recourse to the common.

changes.before: An early marginal note supplies the collect used in the common for a martyr bishop.
changes.after: Prefixed supplement supplies a proper Thomas collect.
changes.locus_before: Lincoln MS 115, early marginal addition to the Collectar; Woolley I, p. xv (PDF 19), compared in p. xix (PDF 23).

evidence.claim: Editor describes the marginal and prefixed states.
Edition prints the proper collect.
Editor describes the marginal and prefixed states.
Edition prints the proper collect.

transitions.limitations: Earlier margin not independently inspected in a manuscript image; evidence level stays scholarly-description.

transitions.summary: The paten gesture at the embolism changes.

evidence.claim: Explicit comparison of the earlier and later ritual.
Explicit comparison of the earlier and later ritual.

transitions.limitations: Intervening history and immediate book ancestry remain unestablished.

transitions.summary: Further sequence reduction follows the 1660 chapter.

changes.before: Selected non-Roman sequences remained after the earlier reform.
changes.after: Only Laetabundus remains outside the Pian repertory.

evidence.claim: The account distinguishes the reforms.
The account distinguishes the reforms.

transitions.limitations: Original printed sequence tables not collated. The earlier sequence selection follows the scholarly reform narrative, not an inspected inventory of the 1622 printing.

transitions.summary: Manuscript and print witness the Windesheim ordinal tradition.

evidence.claim: Explicit catalogue comparison.
Explicit catalogue comparison.

gaps.consequence: Scholarly transitions cannot be promoted to text-collated or exact first implementation.

gaps.consequence: Palaeographic dates, relationships between layers and house attribution remain attributed to the editor.

gaps.next_source: GW M23909; OSZK Inc 176 and RMK III 0196; Cambridge Inc.2.G.8.3[839]; Zagreb RI-4°-63.
